# A host merge in progress no longer masks the report of the page the author
# controls, and no longer refuses a write that attempts no commit. The four
# behaviors below run against one host repository carrying a clean merge.

env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=user.name
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ambient
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=user.email
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ambient@local

mkdir host
cd host
exec git init -q
cp ../base-file.txt base.txt
exec git add base.txt
exec git commit -m 'host base'

exec akb init docs --embed
stdout '^Initialized KB "docs" at .*/host/docs$'

# The adr template carries the write-time rules the pin below fails and the
# valid page satisfies.
cd docs
exec akb template get adr --full --examples
cp stdout .agent-kb/templates/adr.yaml
exec akb template get adr --example --examples
cp stdout .agent-kb/templates/adr_pass.md
exec git add .agent-kb/templates
exec git commit -m 'seed adr template'

# Both branches advance, so the merge is a real one; --no-commit stops it
# cleanly, with no conflict to resolve.
cd $WORK/host
exec git checkout -b feature
cp ../feature-file.txt feature.txt
exec git add feature.txt
exec git commit -m 'feature work'
exec git checkout -
cp ../base-advance.txt base.txt
exec git add base.txt
exec git commit -m 'advance the base branch'
exec git merge --no-commit feature

cd docs
exec git rev-parse HEAD
cp stdout head-before.txt

# (a) The page's own rules are evaluated first, so a page that fails them
# reports the rules it failed and exits 1 — not the merge refusal, which would
# exit 2 and hide the rules behind the state of the repository.
stdin ../../invalid-adr.md
exec bash -c 'akb write adr/missing-context.md; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=1$'
stderr '\[require_context\] page must have a .## Context. heading'
! stderr 'merge in progress'
! stderr 'usage:'
! exists kb/decisions/adr/missing-context.md

# (b) A write that leaves its commit to the caller attempts no commit, so the
# merge is not its precondition: the page is written and HEAD does not move.
stdin ../../valid-adr.md
exec bash -c 'akb write adr/no-commit-write.md --no-commit; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=0$'
stdout '^Written to kb/decisions/adr/no-commit-write\.md$'
exists kb/decisions/adr/no-commit-write.md
exec git rev-parse HEAD
cmp stdout head-before.txt

# The write reaches the working tree only: the page is untracked in the
# merging host repository and git's index never records it.
cd $WORK/host
exec git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- docs/kb/decisions/adr/no-commit-write.md
stdout '^\?\? docs/kb/decisions/adr/no-commit-write\.md$'
! exec git ls-files --error-unmatch docs/kb/decisions/adr/no-commit-write.md
cd docs

# (c) A committing write still refuses before writing: the merge belongs to the
# host project, and the refusal names that repository and that merge.
stdin ../../valid-adr.md
exec bash -c 'akb write adr/refused-write.md; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=2$'
stderr '^usage: write page: merge in progress in repository '${WORK@R}'/host \(outside the knowledge base, in: [^)]+\): akb commits are blocked until it is completed or aborted\. This merge belongs to the host project — do not resolve it from the KB; retry later or surface to the user\.$'
! stderr 'internal:'
! exists kb/decisions/adr/refused-write.md

# (d) A command whose preflight sits immediately before its mutation reports
# the precondition it reached first: the page it was asked to delete, not the
# merge that would have guarded the commit of a successful delete.
exec bash -c 'akb delete notes/nope.md; echo "akb-exit=$?"'
stdout '^akb-exit=1$'
stderr 'page not found: notes/nope\.md\. Use .akb list. to see available pages'
! stderr 'merge in progress'

-- base-file.txt --
The host project's base revision.
-- base-advance.txt --
The host project advanced its base branch.
-- feature-file.txt --
The host project's feature work.
-- invalid-adr.md --
---
type: adr
title: Missing Context
summary: ADR without context section
tags: [test]
status: proposed
deciders: team
created: "2026-01-01"
updated: "2026-09-01"
---

# Missing Context

## Decision

We decided something.
-- valid-adr.md --
---
type: adr
title: Use SQLite for the Index
summary: We decided to keep the search index in SQLite so it stays rebuildable from the pages alone.
tags: [search, sqlite]
status: proposed
deciders: akb maintainers
created: 2026-01-01
updated: 2026-01-02
---

# Use SQLite for the Index

## Context

Every page is a markdown file on disk, so the search index has to be rebuildable from those files alone. The background notes for the storage layer live in [[sqlite-notes]], and the ranking behavior behind the choice is described there in more detail than this record needs to repeat.

## Decision

Use SQLite with FTS5 as the single search index beside the knowledge base.

## Consequences

Full-text search is fast and the index is a single file that travels with the base. A rebuild re-derives the whole index from the page bodies without touching the pages themselves.
